title: Local relative homotopy lifts from isomorphisms on homotopy sheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], equipped with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves. A sieve on $V$ is a collection of arrows into $V$ closed under precomposition; the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. Use simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and associated sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Write $\Delta^n=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(-,[n])$ and let $\partial\Delta^n$ be its union of proper faces, empty for $n=0$. A Kan complex has fillers for every horn, where a horn $\Lambda_i^q$ is the union of all faces except the $i$th, $q\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq q$. Let $F,G:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}$ have Kan values and let $f:F\to G$ be a natural transformation. Let $\pi_0F$ denote the presheaf of components. For $V\in\mathcal C$, a vertex $x\in F(V)_0$ and $m\geq1$, write $\pi_m(F,x)$ for the presheaf on $\mathcal C/V$ sending $u:W\to V$ to the based simplicial homotopy group $\pi_m(F(W),u^*x)$, and similarly for $G,f(x)$; the slice has the induced covering-sieve topology. Suppose $\pi_0F\to\pi_0G$ and all these maps $\pi_m(F,x)\to\pi_m(G,f(x))$ induce isomorphisms on associated sheaves. Then, for every $V\in\mathcal C$, $n\geq0$ and maps $a:\partial\Delta^n\to F(V)$ and $b:\Delta^n\to G(V)$ with $f_Va=b|_{\partial\Delta^n}$, there is a covering sieve $S$ on $V$ such that for every $u:W\to V$ in $S$ there are simplicial maps
$$c_u:\Delta^n\to F(W),\qquad H_u:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to G(W)$$
satisfying
$$c_u|_{\partial\Delta^n}=u^*a,\qquad H_u(-,0)=f_Wc_u,\qquad H_u(-,1)=u^*b,\qquad H_u|_{\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^1}=(f_Wu^*a)\operatorname{pr}_1.$$
No local fibration hypothesis on $f$ is assumed, and the choices for different $u$ need not agree.

source.place: Dugger--Isaksen, Weak equivalences of simplicial presheaves, Definition 3.1, Definition 6.11 and Theorem 6.15(a), printed pp. 4, 13-14; homotopy-sheaf formulation Proposition 6.9. Also DHI arXiv:math/0205027v2 Proposition 3.1, printed p. 7. Objectwise Kan specialization of the locally fibrant theorem, forward direction. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-presheaf homotopy-lifting theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] to $\pi_0F\to\pi_0G$ on $\mathcal C$ and to every based homotopy-presheaf map on its slice. Thus a class in the target locally has a preimage, and two source classes with equal images locally agree. Use the pointed simplex model in [def-cbc-local-simplicial-presheaf-maps]: for $r\geq1$, $S^r=\Delta^r/\partial\Delta^r$ and $\pi_r(Z,x)$ consists of maps $(S^r,*)\to(Z,x)$ modulo based simplicial homotopy. All restrictions preserve the chosen vertex, since $f(u^*x)=u^*f(x)$. The local bijectivity criterion is applied on the relevant slice itself, not by assuming the site has enough points.

source.place: Lemma 6.8 and Proposition 6.9; Section 2, pointed simplex convention.

proof.text:
Here is the objectwise Kan calculus used below. For a monomorphism $K\hookrightarrow L$ and Kan $Z$, [lem-cbc-internal-hom-fibration-corner-map], with $Z\to *$, says that restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(L,Z)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,Z)$ is a Kan fibration. Consequently a homotopy on $K$ extends to $L$ whenever its starting map on $L$ is supplied: lift its edge through this fibration. The same theorem with empty $K$ says the mapping spaces are Kan, and their fixed-restriction fibres are Kan by pulling back the horn-lifting property. In such a fibre an edge can be reversed by filling the $2$-horn consisting of that edge and an identity, and two edges can be composed by filling the corresponding $2$-horn. Thus a finite chain of homotopies with a fixed restriction is a single homotopy, in either orientation. In particular a simplicially nullhomotopic map $K\to Z$ extends over any monomorphism $K\hookrightarrow L$: lift a homotopy from the constant map (which extends) to that map.

We also need nullhomotopies with a chosen vertex fixed. If $M$ is weakly contractible and $t:*\hookrightarrow M$ is a vertex, [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance] makes restriction $t^*:\operatorname{Fun}(M,Z)\to Z$ a simplicial homotopy equivalence. It is therefore a weak equivalence by [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak], and it is a fibration by the corner-map theorem. The model axioms of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] make it a trivial fibration. Its fibre over $x$ lifts every boundary, including $\partial\Delta^1$, so any pointed map $(M,t)\to(Z,x)$ is homotopic to the constant map through maps fixing $t$. These facts apply to horns, simplices, and the contractible quotients used below; no presheaf map is being assumed a fibration.

source.place: Lemma 2.1 and Proposition 3.6: explicit objectwise prism and nullhomotopy arguments, using existing Kan model tools.

proof.text: We spell out invariance under a homotopy of the entire square. Suppose $i:K\hookrightarrow L$ and maps $A:K\times\Delta^1\to X$, $B:L\times\Delta^1\to Y$ satisfy $fA=B|_{K\times\Delta^1}$, with $X,Y$ Kan. Given a relative homotopy lift $c_0:L\to X$ of the time-zero square, extend $(c_0,A)$ to $C:L\times\Delta^1\to X$ by the restriction fibration of [lem-cbc-internal-hom-fibration-corner-map]. Put $R=(L\times\Delta^1)\amalg_{K\times\Delta^1}K$ and $T=L\amalg_K L\subseteq R$. The homotopy $fC$ on one copy of $L$ and $B$ on the other give a homotopy $T\times\Delta^1\to Y$, compatible on $K$. At its time-zero end the given relative homotopy is a map $R\to Y$. Extend this map and that homotopy across $R\times\Delta^1$ by the restriction fibration for $T\hookrightarrow R$. At time one its restriction is a homotopy $fc_1\simeq B_1$ relative to $K$, where $c_1=C_1$ and $c_1|_K=A_1$. For the reverse implication, the simplicial set of commutative squares is $\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,Y)}\operatorname{Fun}(L,Y)$. It is Kan: its projection to $\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)$ is the pullback of the restriction fibration for $K\hookrightarrow L$, and its base is Kan. Invert the edge $(A,B)$ in this Kan complex and apply the same construction. This proves the reverse implication with compatible homotopies in both rows. This construction is objectwise and survives restriction to any covering arrow.

source.place: Proposition 3.6, including the relative cylinder R and the second prism extension.

proof.text: For $n=0$, step 1 gives a covering sieve on which the component of the vertex $b$ is represented by a vertex $c$ of $F$. The equality here is already equality in the ordinary component set of $G(W)$: the image of $[c]$ equals $[b|_W]$. A component is generated by edges, and the Kan horn compositions and inverses of step 2 turn such a finite chain into one edge from $f(c)$ to $b|_W$. This is the required $H:\Delta^0\times\Delta^1\to G(W)$. No based positive-dimensional group and no boundary condition is used.

source.place: Theorem 5.2, first sentence, localized by Lemma 6.8; Theorem 6.15(a).

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$, put $D=\Delta^n$, $K=\partial\Delta^n$, and $A=\Lambda_n^n\subseteq K$. Choose its vertex $n$ (the cone vertex of this horn, also when $n=1$). The horn inclusion $A\hookrightarrow D$ is a trivial cofibration in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core], and $D$ contracts to its vertex $n$ by the simplicial homotopy induced by $[n]\times[1]\to[n]$, $(i,0)\mapsto i$, $(i,1)\mapsto n$, so $\Delta^0\to D$ at that vertex is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak]; by two-out-of-three $A$ is weakly contractible. Step 2 gives a homotopy of $a|_A$ to the constant vertex $x=a(n)$, fixed at that vertex. Extend it to $K$ in $F(V)$ by [lem-cbc-internal-hom-fibration-corner-map], starting with $a$. Extend its image under $f$ to $D$ in $G(V)$ by that same theorem, starting with $b$. We obtain a homotopy of squares from $(a,b)$ to $(a',b')$, where $a'|_A=x$. Thus $a'$ and $b'$ factor through $B=K/A$ and $Q=D/A$. Directly from the face identifications, $B$ is $S^{n-1}=\Delta^{n-1}/\partial\Delta^{n-1}$ for $n\geq2$; for $n=1$ it is the pointed two-vertex set $S^0$. The inclusion $*\hookrightarrow Q$ is the cobase change of the horn inclusion $A\hookrightarrow D$, hence a trivial cofibration by the model axioms, so $Q$ is weakly contractible. By step 3 it suffices to lift this normalized square; we will then undo the homotopy of squares.

source.place: Theorem 5.2, first reduction; Lemma 5.1, horn collapse. The quotient B is checked separately when n=1.

proof.text: For $n\geq2$, write $g:B\to F(V)$ and $h:Q\to G(V)$ for the normalized maps. The based map $h$ is homotopic to the constant map at $f(x)$ with the vertex of $Q$ fixed, by step 2, since $Q$ is weakly contractible. Hence $[fg]=0$ in $\pi_{n-1}(G(V),f(x))$. Local injectivity from [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] gives, on a covering sieve, $[g]=0$ in $\pi_{n-1}(F(W),x|_W)$. The pointed simplex convention [def-cbc-local-simplicial-presheaf-maps] and the fixed-restriction Kan fibre in step 2 turn this equality into a based simplicial nullhomotopy. Lift its reverse through $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,F(W))\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,F(W))$, starting with the constant map. Its endpoint is a map $l:Q\to F(W)$ with $l|_B=g$ exactly. For $n=1$, the images under $f$ of the two vertices of $B=S^0$ lie in the same component because $h:Q=\Delta^1\to G(V)$ joins them. Local injectivity on $\pi_0$ makes their components in $F$ agree locally. Kan horn composition gives an edge $l:\Delta^1\to F(W)$ between those prescribed vertices, again with $l|_B=g$. This treats n=1 without introducing a nonexistent based group in degree zero.

source.place: Theorem 5.2, extension over the contractible quotient; Lemmas 2.1 and 6.8. Separate pi_0 argument in degree one.

proof.text: We need the following auxiliary construction, for $r\geq2$. Consider a square $j:\Lambda_r^r\to F(W)$, $k:\partial\Delta^r\to G(W)$ with $fj=k|_{\Lambda_r^r}$. It has a local homotopy lift relative to the horn using only surjectivity on $\pi_{r-1}$. Indeed the horn is weakly contractible by the model argument of step 5. Contract $j$ to its value $z$ at vertex $r$ using step 2; extend its image to a homotopy on $\partial\Delta^r$ by [lem-cbc-internal-hom-fibration-corner-map]. At the endpoint $k'$ factors as a pointed map $\partial\Delta^r/\Lambda_r^r=S^{r-1}\to G(W)$. Apply local surjectivity from [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] to its class in $\pi_{r-1}(G(W),f(z))$. On a covering sieve, choose a representative $d:S^{r-1}\to F$ and a based simplicial homotopy $fd\simeq k'$, using [def-cbc-local-simplicial-presheaf-maps] and the fixed-restriction Kan fibre of step 2. Precompose with the quotient to obtain the normalized lift of $\partial\Delta^r$ and a homotopy fixed on the horn. Undo the homotopy of this square by the explicit construction in step 3. This gives a map $m:\partial\Delta^r\to F$ with $m|_{\Lambda_r^r}=j$ and a homotopy $fm\simeq k$ fixed on $\Lambda_r^r$. This is an argument inside the present proof, not an appeal to the local acyclic-fibration child.

source.place: Lemma 5.1, with its homotopy-of-squares reduction written out; localized by Lemma 6.8.

proof.text: On each object where step 6 supplied $l$, regard $l$ and $h$ as maps on $\Delta^n$ constant on $\Lambda_n^n$. Define $k:\partial\Delta^{n+1}\to G$ by taking face $n+1$ to be $h$, face $n$ to be $fl$, and every face $i<n$ to be the constant map at $f(x)$. Define $j:\Lambda_{n+1}^{n+1}\to F$ by face $n$ equal to $l$ and faces $i<n$ constant at $x$. All intersections involving a face $i<n$ are constant, and the intersection of faces $n,n+1$ agrees because $fl$ and $h$ agree on $B$. Thus these are well-defined maps with $fj=k|_{\Lambda_{n+1}^{n+1}}$. Apply step 7 with $r=n+1\geq2$ and obtain, after another covering refinement, $m:\partial\Delta^{n+1}\to F$ and $fm\simeq k$ fixed on that horn. Its face $n+1$ is a simplex $c'$. For $i<n$, the simplicial identity gives $d_i c'=d_n d_i m=x$; for $i=n$ it gives $d_n c'=d_n d_n m=d_n l$. These are exactly the faces of $a'$. The restriction of the homotopy to face $n+1$ joins $fc'$ to $h$ and is constant on the entire boundary of that face, since that boundary belongs to the horn. Hence $(c',H')$ solves the normalized square. Undo its homotopy of squares using step 3 to get $c$ with boundary $a$ and $H$ from $fc$ to $b$, fixed at $fa$ on the boundary.

source.place: Theorem 5.2, final face construction, including the boundary face identities; Proposition 3.6; Theorem 6.15(a).

proof.text: For the fixed value of $n$, the preceding construction uses one local surjectivity of $\pi_0$ when $n=0$, or one local injectivity in degree $n-1$ (degree zero if $n=1$) followed by one local surjectivity in degree $n$. A covering sieve on a slice object is a covering sieve on its underlying domain by the induced topology. If $R$ is the first covering sieve and $R_u$ is a covering sieve on the domain of each $u\in R$, the sieve generated by composites $uv$ with $v\in R_u$ covers by transitivity. Every arrow in it has a factorization through such a composite; restrict the constructed maps along the remaining factor. Naturality preserves all four identities, so the sieve of arrows admitting a solution is itself covering. This proves exactly the asserted existence separately for every arrow in one covering sieve. It takes no common refinement over all integers n and makes no compatibility claim for the chosen solutions.

source.place: Convention 6.4 and Theorem 6.15(a), finite localizations; covering-sieve axioms in the statement.
